subject: vintage

qds.name: QdS, Vino siciliano, buona vendemmia ma produzione in calo (2019)
qds.note: Read directly. Quotes Assovini Sicilia president Alessio Planeta and Coldiretti. Mid-harvest, not final.

donnafugata.name: Donnafugata, The 2019 Donnafugata grape harvest
donnafugata.note: Read directly. Covers Contessa Entellina, Pantelleria, Vittoria and Etna.

doc-sicilia.name: DOC Sicilia Consortium early 2019 harvest estimate (via La Sicilia / Pressflex reports)
doc-sicilia.note: Page text did not load. Figure of up to 30% less is from a search summary only.

claims.claim: Spring was cold and windy in places. Donnafugata names the cold spring as the main cause of smaller crops at Contessa Entellina, Pantelleria and Vittoria.
Rain at Contessa Entellina (west) was 546 mm against a 660 mm average, mostly in winter and spring with a dry summer. Vittoria (south-east) was slightly above average, mostly in spring.
Contrary to forecasts of intense heat, summer was cool with good day to night swings. Early September rain lowered temperatures and helped late varieties finish ripening.
claims.note: QdS describes the island broadly. Donnafugata says Etna was cool. Planeta's estate separately reported an early August heatwave (search summary only), so heat was brief if present.

claims.claim: Frost, hail and flowering were not described for Sicily as a whole in any source read.
Harvest ran about 15 days late overall, mid-harvest. The island's harvest normally lasts around 100 days.
claims.note: One source, Assovini president quoted at mid-harvest.

claims.claim: Sparkling base grapes were picked early. At Contessa Entellina, Donnafugata began on 7 or 8 August with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir for sparkling wine. White picking there ended 26 September, and reds ran late August to September.
claims.note: One producer. Pinot Noir for sparkling base is the grape most relevant to a sparkling rosé.

claims.claim: Other Donnafugata dates: Pantelleria Zibibbo 19 August to 12 September. Vittoria Frappato 20 September to 3 October and Nero d'Avola 21 September to 2 October. Etna Carricante 30 September to 10 October, Nerello Mascalese from 5 October for rosé and 14 to 21 October for reds.

Yields were down. Assovini's president put the average drop at up to 20% mid-harvest. Coldiretti reported Sicilian wine production about 20% lower, around 3.76 million hectolitres. The DOC Sicilia consortium's early estimate was up to 30% less.
claims.note: Two sources agree on a smaller crop, figure varies 20 to 30%. Quote is Planeta on grape quality.

claims.claim: Quality was reported as excellent. Donnafugata calls its Etna whites and rosés particularly fragrant with excellent acid structure, and the Etna reds very elegant with extremely fine tannin.
claims.quote: very elegant and have an extremely fine and well integrated tannin
claims.note: Producer language, plus the Assovini president's view.

claims.claim: Overall a smaller but high-quality year with fresh acidity. No critic vintage rating for Sicily 2019 was read.

conflicts: Yield loss: up to 20% (Assovini president, Coldiretti about 20%) versus up to 30% (DOC Sicilia consortium early estimate, search summary). Early estimates, made before harvest finished.
Timing: harvest described as 15 days late overall, yet sparkling bases began 7 to 8 August at Donnafugata. These are different grapes; early sparkling picks are normal.
gaps: No final Assovini Sicilia or Regione Siciliana report with final hectolitres.
Frost, hail and flowering not described.
DOC Sicilia consortium page could not be read; the 30% figure is from a search summary.

sheet.vintage: 2019 was a smaller crop in Sicily, with a cold spring and a cool summer. Harvest ran late, and the grapes were healthy, fresh and well ripened.
